name: MiMo-V2.6 Pro + Flash
summary: Download open weights that top the open-weight intelligence leaderboards: Pro is a trillion-parameter omnimodal reasoner, Flash is the small MIT-licensed sibling. Xiaomi also published 7,000-plus reinforcement-learning environments and the RL code on Hugging Face.

name: Grok 4.7
summary: Swap in a coding model with a 500K context and four reasoning levels, already wired into Cursor, Grok Build, and the API. Pricing is unchanged from 4.6 at $2 per million input tokens and $6 output.

name: Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash
summary: Feed text, images, audio, or video into one 1M-token context, then have the model plan, call tools, and finish multimedia work such as video editing or summarization. Available through Qwen APIs with OpenAI-compatible calls.

name: Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0
summary: Transcribe noisy calls, recordings, or live audio with timestamps, speaker labels, keyword biasing, and automatic language switching. The API costs $0.10 per hour for batch or $0.20 for streaming, making searchable video and voice features cheap to ship.

name: Bonsai 2 27B
summary: Run a 27B reasoning, coding, and vision model on a laptop: ternary weights squeeze it to 5.9GB while keeping 98% of full-precision scores. It has 262K context, Apache 2.0 weights on Hugging Face, and MLX builds for Mac and iPhone plus CUDA.

name: Claude Docs + Slides
summary: Ask for a doc or deck in a normal chat and get an editable document or presentation you can revise in place, present, or export to Word, PowerPoint, or PDF. Cowork is folded into chat too, with Pro and Max access first.

name: Gemini 3.8 Live
summary: Build voice agents that reason and talk at once, call functions in the background mid-conversation, and see what the camera sees. Live in the Gemini API and AI Studio at $0.005 per minute in and $0.018 out, plus a new 3.5 Transcribe speech-to-text model.

name: Cline Desktop
summary: Run parallel coding agents from one open-source desktop app, schedule recurring work, and pick from 300-plus hosted or open-weight models. It supports local workspaces, plugins, MCP servers, and skills on macOS and Windows.
